film_movements_doc_exp_short.hint: A1 keeps one leaf per named movement (they are attested canons; small leaves are fine here) but give big movements (New Hollywood, Slow Cinema, French New Wave) sections. A19 Documentary (old A13, 894) must be split by mode and subject into leaves (e.g. observational/direct cinema, essay film, investigative & political documentary, biographical & portrait documentary, music & concert, nature & wildlife, true crime, sports documentary, war & history documentary, art & artist documentary, personal/autobiographical, ethnographic, city symphony, mondo, compilation/archival). A21 Short Film takes the old live-action, documentary and experimental shorts (old B2, B3, B4): split by mode (trick film, actuality, silent comedy short, narrative short by genre, documentary short, avant-garde short ...). Animated shorts are NOT in this block (they go to Animation).

film_crime_thriller.hint: Old A2-4 Crime Drama (352), A2-5 Film Noir & Neo-Noir (250), A2-3 Police & Detective (214), A3-9 Suspense Thriller (247), A3-1 Psychological Thriller (195), A3-7 Spy (172) are catch-alls. Split by plot engine: e.g. classic film noir vs neo-noir; police procedural, private-eye, whodunit/mystery, legal-crime, caper, con-artist, gangster epic, mob, drug-trade, serial-killer thriller, erotic thriller, conspiracy, techno-thriller, cat-and-mouse, hostage & siege, chase, domestic/marriage thriller, stalker, amnesia/identity, Cold War spy, spy-action franchise, giallo, poliziottesco, yakuza, Korean revenge thriller, hood film, blaxploitation ...

film_horror_scifi.hint: Old A4-3 Supernatural Horror (442) and A5-3 Science Fiction Film (220) are catch-alls. Horror by the source of fear: possession & exorcism, demonic/occult & satanic, ghost story, curse, witchcraft, religious horror, haunted house, folk horror, slasher (classic / meta / backwoods), monster movie, werewolf, vampire, zombie, mummy, creature feature, eco-horror, body horror, cosmic/Lovecraftian, psychological horror, home invasion, survival horror, found footage, anthology horror, splatter, torture porn, J-horror, K-horror, Thai horror, Italian gothic, Hammer horror, Universal Classic Monsters, comedy horror, elevated horror, etc. Science fiction by premise: hard SF, space exploration, space opera, alien invasion, first contact, time travel, dystopia, post-apocalyptic, disaster film, cyberpunk, artificial intelligence & robots, genetic engineering/mad science, parallel worlds, kaiju, tokusatsu, social science fiction, B-movie 1950s science fiction ... A5 is renamed Science Fiction (monster films that are horror stay A4; kaiju stays in A5).

film_history_war_western_biopic.hint: Old A7 (Historical, Period & War) and A17 (Western). A11 Biographical Film (old A7-8, 649) must be split by the subject's field: musician biopic, artist & writer biopic, sports biopic, political & royal biopic, scientist & inventor, crime & outlaw biopic, religious figures, entertainment & showbusiness, military, business ... A9 War Film by war and mode (WWI, WWII combat, Holocaust, Pacific war, Vietnam War, anti-war film, POW film, war epic, home front, partisan film, Cold War / modern war, atomic bomb ...). A8 period film: costume drama, heritage film, epic, sword-and-sandal, jidaigeki, chanbara, historical epic, medieval film, royal court drama ... A10 Western: classic, revisionist, spaghetti, acid, neo-western, ostern, contemporary western ...

film_fantasy_action_family_popular.hint: Old A6 (Fantasy Film 272, Superhero 216, Adventure 101), A8 (Action Film 264 ...), A19 (Children's Film 227, Christmas Film 155), A18 (Masala 112, Nollywood, Yeşilçam). Split: superhero by franchise universe / type (MCU, DC, standalone, deconstruction); fantasy (high fantasy, sword and sorcery, dark fantasy, urban fantasy, portal fantasy, mythological, fairy tale, magical realism, fantasy comedy); adventure (jungle adventure, treasure hunt, lost world, sea adventure, swashbuckler); action (action thriller, one-man army, martial arts, wuxia, kung fu, heroic bloodshed, gun fu, buddy cop, disaster action, car chase & heist action, video-game adaptation, girls-with-guns ...); family (family comedy, animal adventure, children's fantasy, holiday/Christmas film by mode, teen adventure ...); masala by industry where the field names it (Telugu masala, Tamil masala, Bollywood masala are attested).

film_comedy.hint: THE MAIN PROBLEM CASE: old A10-1 Comedy Film holds 630 titles from silent films to Zoolander, A10-2 Comedy-Drama 668, A10-3 Black Comedy & Satire 403. Split the whole comic field by comic mode and comic engine into many leaves: silent clown comedy, comedy teams (Marx Brothers, Laurel & Hardy), screwball, comedy of manners, comedy of remarriage, farce & bedroom farce, Ealing comedy, commedia all'italiana, slapstick, gross-out, stoner comedy, frat/college comedy, teen comedy, sex comedy, buddy comedy, road comedy, fish-out-of-water, body-swap & high-concept comedy, family comedy, wedding & holiday comedy, workplace comedy, sports comedy, military comedy, crime comedy & caper, action comedy, spy spoof, parody & spoof, mockumentary, satire (political, media, corporate, social), black comedy, absurdist & surreal comedy, deadpan & quirky indie comedy, cringe comedy, comedy-drama by subject (midlife, family dysfunction, coming-of-age dramedy, illness dramedy), Bourekas, stand-up film, sketch-anthology film ... Zoolander is a fashion-world parody; Animal House a frat comedy. Romantic comedy is NOT in this block (it is in A13 Romance).

film_romance_musical_erotic.hint: Old A9-1 Romantic Drama (687) and A9-2 Romantic Comedy (580) are catch-alls; A11-1 Musical & Music Film (312). Romance by the love-story engine: forbidden/class-crossed love, tragic romance & weepie, wartime romance, period romance (Austen-type heritage romance), brief encounter, second-chance, love triangle, queer romance, teen romance, May-December, epistolary/long-distance, supernatural/fantasy romance; romantic comedy by engine: screwball rom-com, meet-cute, enemies-to-lovers, fake relationship, wedding rom-com, holiday rom-com, workplace rom-com, rom-com of manners, Bollywood romance ... Musical: backstage musical, integrated book musical, jukebox musical, film-opera, rock opera, biopic-musical? (no, biopics are elsewhere), dance film, music-competition film, Bollywood song-and-dance where leaf-worthy, rumberas. Erotic: erotic drama, sexploitation, pink film, Roman Porno (keep leaves even if empty only if they had titles before; Pink Film and Roman Porno had 0 titles — keep them as leaves with a note only if attested canon; the pornographic film leaf is retired and must not appear).

animation_non_japanese.hint: Old A15 (Hand-Drawn 331, Computer-Animated 382, Stop-Motion 43, Adult 71), C6 (Children's Animated Series 278, Action-Adventure 193, Animated Sitcom 134, Adult 37), B1 animated shorts (theatrical cartoon, auteur short, stop-motion, CG, TV special; 250). These are non-Japanese animation (anime is C1–C11). Technique (hand-drawn, CG, stop-motion) is a strong axis but leaves of 380 are too big: organise features by the tradition or cycle the field names and by genre: Disney animated canon by era (Golden Age, Disney Renaissance, Revival), Pixar, DreamWorks Animation, Illumination/family CG comedy, animated musical fairy tale, Don Bluth, Soviet/Soyuzmultfilm, European auteur animation (Franco-Belgian, Cartoon Saloon, Aardman stop-motion), Chinese animation (donghua features), Korean, adult animation, animated documentary, rotoscope, puppet/stop-motion feature (Laika), etc. Studio-defined leaves are acceptable ONLY where the field names the studio's output as a canon (Disney animated canon, Pixar films, Golden Age of American animation). Series: animated sitcom, adult animated series, superhero animated series, action-adventure, preschool, Cartoon Network/Nicktoons era (attested as 'Nicktoons', 'Cartoon Cartoons'), donghua series, European children's series ... Shorts: Golden Age theatrical cartoons (Looney Tunes, Disney shorts, Fleischer), auteur/art shorts (NFB, Zagreb School), stop-motion shorts, CG shorts (Pixar shorts), TV specials.
